key_insight: The paper shows that AI theorem-proving agents can be benchmarked reproducibly on quantum algorithms and quantum information, and that access to a verified domain library materially improves proof success.
engineering_relevance: For quantum software and formal methods teams, this provides a practical baseline for evaluating and strengthening machine-checkable proof agents on domain-specific math and physics tasks.
method: Built two Lean 4 benchmarks: Lean-QuantumAlg-Bench (36 tasks) and Lean-QIT-Bench (40 tasks).
Evaluated four models under two settings: task-only baseline and library-augmented deduction (LAD).
Used fixed-environment compilation, deterministic proof checking, semantic review, and preassigned difficulty weights.
evidence_signal: Across eight model-benchmark comparisons, LAD improved both score and completion rate, with top difficulty-weighted scores reaching 60.4/100 on quantum algorithms and 59.6/100 on quantum information.
watch_item: Results depend on a fixed Lean environment and benchmark-specific libraries, so generalization to broader quantum formalization tasks may be limited.
paper_title: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
